sets.title: Currency exchange outlet
sets.contentHtml:
The base exchange rate of a currency X with respect to a currency Y is the number of units of currency Y which is equivalent in value to one unit of currency X. Currency exchange outlets buy currency at buying exchange rates that are lower than base exchange rates, and sell currency at selling exchange rates that are higher than base exchange rates.

A currency exchange outlet uses the local currency L to buy and sell three international currencies A, B, and C, but does not exchange one international currency directly with another. The base exchange rates of A, B and C with respect to L are in the ratio 100:120:1. The buying exchange rates of each of A, B, and C with respect to L are 5% below the corresponding base exchange rates, and their selling exchange rates are 10% above their corresponding base exchange rates.

The following facts are known about the outlet on a particular day:

  1. The amount of L used by the outlet to buy C equals the amount of L it received by selling C.
  2. The amounts of L used by the outlet to buy A and B are in the ratio 5:3.
  3. The amounts of L the outlet received from the sales of A and B are in the ratio 5:9.
  4. The outlet received 88000 units of L by selling A during the day.
  5. The outlet started the day with some amount of L, 2500 units of A, 4800 units of B, and 48000 units of C.
  6. The outlet ended the day with some amount of L, 3300 units of A, 4800 units of B, and 51000 units of C.

sets.title: Sentence coding scheme
sets.contentHtml:
According to a coding scheme the sentence

Peacock is designated as the national bird of India

is coded as

5688999 35 1135556678 56 458 13666689 1334 79 13366

This coding scheme has the following rules:

  1. The scheme is case-insensitive (does not distinguish between upper case and lower case letters).
  2. Each letter has a unique code which is a single digit from among 1, 2, 3, …, 9.
  3. The digit 9 codes two letters, and every other digit codes three letters.
  4. The code for a word is constructed by arranging the digits corresponding to its letters in a non-decreasing sequence.

sets.title: College accreditation scores
sets.contentHtml:
An agency entrusted to accredit colleges looks at four parameters: faculty quality (F), reputation (R), placement quality (P), and infrastructure (I). The four parameters are used to arrive at an overall score, which the agency uses to give an accreditation to the colleges. In each parameter, there are five possible letter grades given, each carrying certain points: A (50 points), B (40 points), C (30 points), D (20 points), and F (0 points). The overall score for a college is the weighted sum of the points scored in the four parameters. The weights of the parameters are 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 in some order, but the order is not disclosed. Accreditation is awarded based on the following scheme:

RangeAccreditation
Overall score ≥ 45AAA
35 ≤ Overall score < 45BAA
25 ≤ Overall score < 35BBA
15 ≤ Overall score < 25BBB
Overall score < 15Junk

Eight colleges apply for accreditation, and receive the following grades in the four parameters (F, R, P, and I):

CollegeFRPI
A-oneAAAB
Best EdBCDD
CosmopolitanBDDC
DominanceDDBC
Education AidAABA
FancyAABB
GlobalCFDD
High QCDDB

It is further known that in terms of overall scores:

  1. High Q is better than Best Ed;
  2. Best Ed is better than Cosmopolitan; and
  3. Education Aid is better than A-one.

sets.title: Amusement park tickets
sets.contentHtml:
Each visitor to an amusement park needs to buy a ticket. Tickets can be Platinum, Gold, or Economy. Visitors are classified as Old, Middle-aged, or Young. The following facts are known about visitors and ticket sales on a particular day:

  1. 140 tickets were sold.
  2. The number of Middle-aged visitors was twice the number of Old visitors, while the number of Young visitors was twice the number of Middle-aged visitors.
  3. Young visitors bought 38 of the 55 Economy tickets that were sold, and they bought half the total number of Platinum tickets that were sold.
  4. The number of Gold tickets bought by Old visitors was equal to the number of Economy tickets bought by Old visitors.

sets.title: Fun Sports enrolment
sets.contentHtml:
Fun Sports (FS) provides training in three sports – Gilli-danda (G), Kho-Kho (K), and Ludo (L). Currently it has an enrollment of 39 students each of whom is enrolled in at least one of the three sports. The following details are known:

  1. The number of students enrolled only in L is double the number of students enrolled in all the three sports.
  2. There are a total of 17 students enrolled in G.
  3. The number of students enrolled only in G is one less than the number of students enrolled only in L.
  4. The number of students enrolled only in K is equal to the number of students who are enrolled in both K and L.
  5. The maximum student enrollment is in L.
  6. Ten students enrolled in G are also enrolled in at least one more sport.

questions.stemHtml: How many units of currency A did the outlet buy on that day?
questions.solutionHtml:
Set-up: let the base rates be 100k, 120k and k units of L for A, B and C. Buying rates are 0.95 × base (95k, 114k, 0.95k) and selling rates 1.1 × base (110k, 132k, 1.1k).

Sales of A brought 88000 L, so sales of B brought 88000 × 9/5 = 158400 L. Units of B sold = 158400/132k = 1200/k. B's stock is unchanged (4800 → 4800), so the outlet also bought 1200/k units of B, spending 1200/k × 114k = 136800 L.

Spending on A : B = 5 : 3, so 228000 L was spent on A, i.e. 228000/95k = 2400/k units bought. Units of A sold = 88000/110k = 800/k. A's stock rose by 3300 − 2500 = 800, so 2400/k − 800/k = 800, giving k = 2.

So base rates are A = 200, B = 240, C = 2; A bought 1200, A sold 400; B bought = sold = 600.

Units of A bought = 2400/k = 2400/2 = 1200. (Check: 1200 bought − 400 sold = 800 = 3300 − 2500.)

questions.stemHtml: What best can be concluded about the code for the letter L?
questions.solutionHtml:
Decoding: "as" = 56 and "is" = 35 share only s, so s = 5, a = 6, i = 3. "india" = 13366: i, i, a use 3, 3, 6, so n and d are 1 and 6.

"national" = 13666689 has two n's but only one 1, so n = 6, d = 1. Removing n, n, a, a, i leaves 1, 8, 9 for t, o, l.

"designated" = 1135556678: removing d, d, s, i, n, a (1, 1, 5, 3, 6, 6) leaves 5, 5, 7, 8 for e, e, g, t, so e = 5 and {g, t} = {7, 8}. As t ∈ {1, 8, 9}, t = 8, g = 7. "the" = 458 gives h = 4. Now o and l are 1 and 9.

"peacock" = 5688999 has no 1, so o = 9, l = 1. Removing e, a, o leaves 8, 8, 9, 9 for p, c, c, k. If c = 8 then p = k = 9 and 9 would code o, p, k: three letters, not allowed. So c = 9, p = k = 8. "of" = 79 gives f = 7. "bird" = 1334: b and r are 3 and 4 in some order.

Table: 1 → d, l (+1 unknown); 2 → none known; 3 → i (+ b or r); 4 → h (+ b or r); 5 → s, e; 6 → a, n; 7 → f, g; 8 → t, p, k (complete); 9 → o, c (complete).

L is fixed: "peacock" contains o but no digit 1, so o = 9 and l takes the other value from {1, 9}, i.e. L = 1.

questions.stemHtml: For how many digits can the complete list of letters associated with that digit be identified?
questions.solutionHtml:
Decoding: "as" = 56 and "is" = 35 share only s, so s = 5, a = 6, i = 3. "india" = 13366: i, i, a use 3, 3, 6, so n and d are 1 and 6.

"national" = 13666689 has two n's but only one 1, so n = 6, d = 1. Removing n, n, a, a, i leaves 1, 8, 9 for t, o, l.

"designated" = 1135556678: removing d, d, s, i, n, a (1, 1, 5, 3, 6, 6) leaves 5, 5, 7, 8 for e, e, g, t, so e = 5 and {g, t} = {7, 8}. As t ∈ {1, 8, 9}, t = 8, g = 7. "the" = 458 gives h = 4. Now o and l are 1 and 9.

"peacock" = 5688999 has no 1, so o = 9, l = 1. Removing e, a, o leaves 8, 8, 9, 9 for p, c, c, k. If c = 8 then p = k = 9 and 9 would code o, p, k: three letters, not allowed. So c = 9, p = k = 8. "of" = 79 gives f = 7. "bird" = 1334: b and r are 3 and 4 in some order.

Table: 1 → d, l (+1 unknown); 2 → none known; 3 → i (+ b or r); 4 → h (+ b or r); 5 → s, e; 6 → a, n; 7 → f, g; 8 → t, p, k (complete); 9 → o, c (complete).

Digit 8 has its full quota of three letters (t, p, k) and digit 9 its full quota of two (o, c). Every other digit still has at least one unknown letter (for example 5 has only s and e; 3 and 4 are not even settled between b and r). So the answer is 2.

questions.stemHtml: Which set of letters CANNOT be coded with the same digit?
questions.solutionHtml:
Decoding: "as" = 56 and "is" = 35 share only s, so s = 5, a = 6, i = 3. "india" = 13366: i, i, a use 3, 3, 6, so n and d are 1 and 6.

"national" = 13666689 has two n's but only one 1, so n = 6, d = 1. Removing n, n, a, a, i leaves 1, 8, 9 for t, o, l.

"designated" = 1135556678: removing d, d, s, i, n, a (1, 1, 5, 3, 6, 6) leaves 5, 5, 7, 8 for e, e, g, t, so e = 5 and {g, t} = {7, 8}. As t ∈ {1, 8, 9}, t = 8, g = 7. "the" = 458 gives h = 4. Now o and l are 1 and 9.

"peacock" = 5688999 has no 1, so o = 9, l = 1. Removing e, a, o leaves 8, 8, 9, 9 for p, c, c, k. If c = 8 then p = k = 9 and 9 would code o, p, k: three letters, not allowed. So c = 9, p = k = 8. "of" = 79 gives f = 7. "bird" = 1334: b and r are 3 and 4 in some order.

Table: 1 → d, l (+1 unknown); 2 → none known; 3 → i (+ b or r); 4 → h (+ b or r); 5 → s, e; 6 → a, n; 7 → f, g; 8 → t, p, k (complete); 9 → o, c (complete).

S = 5, and 5 already codes s and e, leaving room for only one more letter. U and V cannot both be 5, so S, U, V cannot share a digit.

The others are possible: X, Y, Z could all be 2 (no letters yet); I, B, M could all be 3 if b = 3; S, E, Z could all be 5 with z as the third letter.

questions.stemHtml: The brand that had the highest revenue in 2016 is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Take 100 units sold in 2016 (prices in Rs. thousand). Revenue = share × price: Azra 40 × 15 = 600, Bysi 25 × 20 = 500, Cxqi 15 × 30 = 450, Dipq 20 × 25 = 500.

Profit = revenue × profitability: Azra 60, Bysi 150, Cxqi 180, Dipq 150.

Highest 2016 revenue: Azra (600).

questions.stemHtml: The brand that had the highest profit in 2017 is:

2017: 140 units in all. The shares change by percentage points (they must still add to 100): Cxqi 15 + 15 = 30%, Azra 35%, Bysi 20%, Dipq 15%. Units: Azra 49, Bysi 28, Cxqi 42, Dipq 21. Cxqi's price is 30 × 0.6 = 18 and its profitability 20%.

Balaram is third in Room 101, so 101 has at least 3 people: it must be Fatima's room, i.e. 101 = Akil, ?, Balaram (3rd), Fatima (4th). Erina is alone in 103. So 102 = Ganeshan and Chitra, with Ganeshan before 7:30, and the fourth person in 101 is Divya.

questions.stemHtml: What is the weight of the faculty quality parameter?
questions.solutionHtml:
Finding the weights (wF, wR, wP, wI):

Best Ed (40, 30, 20, 20) > Cosmopolitan (40, 20, 20, 30) gives 10wR > 10wI, so wR > wI. Education Aid (50, 50, 40, 50) > A-one (50, 50, 50, 40) gives wI > wP. High Q (30, 20, 20, 40) > Best Ed (40, 30, 20, 20) gives 20wI > 10wF + 10wR, i.e. 2wI > wF + wR.

With wR > wI > wP, try each value of wF: only wF = 0.1, wR = 0.4, wI = 0.3, wP = 0.2 satisfies 2wI > wF + wR (0.6 > 0.5). For example wF = 0.2 forces R, I, P = 0.4, 0.3, 0.1 and 0.6 > 0.6 fails.

Scores: A-one 47, Best Ed 26, Cosmopolitan 25, Dominance 27, Education Aid 48, Fancy 45, Global 13, High Q 27.

Faculty weight = 0.1.

questions.stemHtml: If the number of Old visitors buying Platinum tickets was equal to the number of Middle-aged visitors buying Platinum tickets, then which among the following could be the total number of Platinum tickets sold?
questions.solutionHtml:
Base grid: Old : Middle : Young = 1 : 2 : 4 with 140 in all, so Old 20, Middle 40, Young 80. Let Old buy x Gold and x Economy, so Old Platinum = 20 − 2x. Economy: Middle buy 55 − 38 − x = 17 − x. Let total Platinum = 2p; Young buy p Platinum, so Young Gold = 80 − 38 − p = 42 − p, and Old + Middle Platinum = p.

Old Platinum = Middle Platinum = p/2, so total Platinum 2p is a multiple of 4: 32 or 36. Old: p/2 + 2x = 20.

Total 36: Old Platinum 9, 2x = 11, not an integer. Total 32: Old Platinum 8, x = 6. Then Middle: Platinum 8, Economy 11, Gold 21; Young: Platinum 16, Economy 38, Gold 26. Everything is consistent, so 32.

questions.stemHtml: If the number of Old visitors buying Gold tickets was strictly greater than the number of Young visitors buying Gold tickets, then the number of Middle-aged visitors buying Gold tickets was
questions.solutionHtml:
Base grid: Old : Middle : Young = 1 : 2 : 4 with 140 in all, so Old 20, Middle 40, Young 80. Let Old buy x Gold and x Economy, so Old Platinum = 20 − 2x. Economy: Middle buy 55 − 38 − x = 17 − x. Let total Platinum = 2p; Young buy p Platinum, so Young Gold = 80 − 38 − p = 42 − p, and Old + Middle Platinum = p.

Middle Platinum = p − (20 − 2x) and Middle Economy = 17 − x, so Middle Gold = 40 − (p − 20 + 2x) − (17 − x) = 43 − p − x.

Condition: Old Gold > Young Gold, i.e. x > 42 − p, so p + x ≥ 43. But Middle Gold = 43 − (p + x) cannot be negative, so p + x = 43 and Middle Gold = 0.

questions.stemHtml: What is the minimum number of students enrolled in both G and L but not in K?
questions.solutionHtml:
Venn set-up: only G = g, only K = k, only L = l, G&K only = a, G&L only = b, K&L only = c, all three = t.

Fact 6: a + b + t = 10, so g = 17 − 10 = 7. Fact 3: l = 8. Fact 1: t = 4. Total 39: 7 + 8 + 10 + k + c = 39, so k + c = 14. Fact 4 (K and L includes the all-three group): k = c + 4, so c = 5, k = 9, and a + b = 6.

Totals: G = 17, K = 9 + a + 5 + 4 = 18 + a, L = 8 + b + 5 + 4 = 17 + b = 23 − a. Fact 5 (L is the largest): 23 − a > 18 + a gives a ≤ 2, so (a, b) = (0, 6), (1, 5) or (2, 4).

b = 6 − a with a ≤ 2, so the minimum is b = 4.

questions.stemHtml: If the numbers of students enrolled in K and L are in the ratio 19:22, then what is the number of students enrolled in L?
questions.solutionHtml:
Venn set-up: only G = g, only K = k, only L = l, G&K only = a, G&L only = b, K&L only = c, all three = t.

Fact 6: a + b + t = 10, so g = 17 − 10 = 7. Fact 3: l = 8. Fact 1: t = 4. Total 39: 7 + 8 + 10 + k + c = 39, so k + c = 14. Fact 4 (K and L includes the all-three group): k = c + 4, so c = 5, k = 9, and a + b = 6.

Totals: G = 17, K = 9 + a + 5 + 4 = 18 + a, L = 8 + b + 5 + 4 = 17 + b = 23 − a. Fact 5 (L is the largest): 23 − a > 18 + a gives a ≤ 2, so (a, b) = (0, 6), (1, 5) or (2, 4).

(18 + a)/(23 − a) = 19/22 gives 396 + 22a = 437 − 19a, so a = 1. L = 23 − 1 = 22 (K = 19).

questions.stemHtml: Due to academic pressure, students who were enrolled in all three sports were asked to withdraw from one of the three sports. After the withdrawal, the number of students enrolled in G was six less than the number of students enrolled in L, while the number of students enrolled in K went down by one. After the withdrawal, how many students were enrolled in both G and K?
questions.solutionHtml:
Venn set-up: only G = g, only K = k, only L = l, G&K only = a, G&L only = b, K&L only = c, all three = t.

Fact 6: a + b + t = 10, so g = 17 − 10 = 7. Fact 3: l = 8. Fact 1: t = 4. Total 39: 7 + 8 + 10 + k + c = 39, so k + c = 14. Fact 4 (K and L includes the all-three group): k = c + 4, so c = 5, k = 9, and a + b = 6.

Totals: G = 17, K = 9 + a + 5 + 4 = 18 + a, L = 8 + b + 5 + 4 = 17 + b = 23 − a. Fact 5 (L is the largest): 23 − a > 18 + a gives a ≤ 2, so (a, b) = (0, 6), (1, 5) or (2, 4).

After withdrawal: each of the 4 all-three students drops one sport. K falls by 1, so exactly 1 drops K (moves to G&L); the other 3 drop G (p of them) or L (q of them), p + q = 3.

New G = 17 − p and new L = 23 − a − q. G = L − 6 gives 17 − p = 17 − a − q, so p − q = a. With p + q = 3 and a ≤ 2, p − q must be odd, so a = 1, p = 2, q = 1.

G and K after withdrawal = a + (those who dropped L) = 1 + 1 = 2.
